history.period: Modern local shrine; described by listing sites as one of the oldest temples in Dewas city (unverified)
history.summary: The Kaila Devi temple stands on Kaila Devi Road in Mishrilal Nagar, Dewas, about 1 km from Dewas railway station. Local lore reported by devotees says the goddess herself wished to come to Dewas, which is why this shrine was established. It is a distinct, smaller shrine and must not be confused with the famous Kaila Devi temple at Karauli, Rajasthan. No published founding date, builder, or architectural history exists online; the CSV town 'Dewas' is correct. The shrine campus also hosts large idols of Hanuman and Durga and a Shiva temple, and TripAdvisor reviewers describe the saffron-coloured Kaila Devi idol as the principal deity.

name: Kaila Devi Temple
town_description: Dewas is a city in Madhya Pradesh about 35 km north of Indore, known for the Tekri hill topped by the Chamunda and Tulja Bhavani shrines, the Kailadevi temple, and its classical-music heritage (Kumar Gandharva).

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (about 40 km)
travel.road: On Kaila Devi Road, Mishrilal Nagar, Dewas; well connected by road to Indore and Ujjain
